confirmed.title: A line manager or Head of Department can see, clear and dismiss alerts about themselves, and that closure stops the evidence from ever raising again
confirmed.scenario: In this codebase `team` scope includes the caller (grants-cache getTeamEmployeeIds starts the recursion at the caller's own employee_id). 1199 grants `alerts.clear` to the manager role, and 0290 gives manager `people` view and approve at team scope. So Musa, a manager, is late 3 times in 30 days. The late_arrivals rule (default permission_key people.view) raises an alert with subject_employee_id = Musa. seenWhere (alerts.repo.js:51-60) puts that alert in his own list, Needs You and the Overview's alerts_to_clear. present() sets can_clear=true. mayClear(..., subject=Musa) returns true; I confirmed this with a probe against mycity_e_test. Musa can then POST /home/alerts/:id/clear with outcome dismissed. dealtWith() counts any closure with cleared_by set, so the sweep never raises that evidence again, and HR with all scope only finds it under View Dismissed. The same applies to approval_ageing (people.approve, team) for his own pending leave request. Attendance refuses exactly this for exceptions (attendance.reconcile.js:137, OWN_RECORD).
confirmed.fix: Refuse self-clearing in the engine: in mayClear, return false when subjectEmployeeId && subjectEmployeeId === user.employee_id and the user is not the CEO (mirroring OWN_RECORD). Make present() compute can_clear the same way, so an alert about the reader shows read-only. Then decide in home.md §6/§8 whether the subject should see their own alert at all, and if not, add `AND a.subject_employee_id IS DISTINCT FROM <reader employee>` to seenWhere.
fixes:
Keep "one definition" by excluding the reader's own alerts from what they see and may clear, except for the CEO.

1. **Engine.** In src/shared/alerts/alerts.js `mayClear`, after the `is_ceo` early return and the `granted` check, add:
   `if (subjectEmployeeId && user.employee_id && subjectEmployeeId === user.employee_id) return false;`
   This mirrors attendance's `OWN_RECORD`. Also correct the comment at line 286, since `own` scope then clears nothing about others.
2. **Reader.** In src/modules/alerts/alerts.service.js `readerOf`, return `seen: { all: false, grants, self: user.employee_id || null }`.
3. **SQL.** In alerts.repo.js `seenWhere`, when `seen.self` is set, push it and wrap the result: `(<parts>) AND a.subject_employee_id IS DISTINCT FROM $n`. The list, alertById (so a self clear is a 404), counts, needs_you, `alerts_to_clear`, the Open High Alerts card, search and the assistant then all agree with mayClear, and `can_clear` needs no extra test.
4. **Guide.** Add a line to home.md §6 "Who sees an alert" and §8: "never an alert about themselves; the CEO excepted, as for approvals and attendance exceptions".
5. **Tests.** Add an integration case where the manager is the subject of a `late_arrivals` alert: it is absent from their list and counts, and their clear gets a 404 (and the engine returns false).

1. **Refuse self-clearing in the engine.** In src/shared/alerts/alerts.js `mayClear`, after the CEO short-circuit (line 274), add:

   `if (subjectEmployeeId && user.employee_id && subjectEmployeeId === user.employee_id) return false;`

   This mirrors attendance OWN_RECORD and the workflow approvers rule. `clear()` then answers 403 "You cannot clear this alert" for the subject. The alert stays visible to them, read-only, and opens in their own view.

2. **Make the row match.** In alerts.service.js `present()`, compute:

   `can_clear: row.cleared_at === null && reader.may_clear && !(row.subject_employee_id && row.subject_employee_id === reader.user.employee_id && !reader.user.is_ceo)`

   Without this the screen offers Clear Alert and then gets a 403.

3. **Keep the counts consistent.** Exclude self-subject alerts from the "mine" / Needs You count and from the Overview's `alerts_to_clear`. Do it by adding `AND a.subject_employee_id IS DISTINCT FROM $reader` only when `mine` is set (and in those counts), not in `seenWhere`, so the person still sees alerts about themselves.

4. **Write it down.** Add one line to home.md §6 "Clearing needs both checks": "nobody but the CEO clears or dismisses an alert about themselves". Add a test where the line manager is the subject of a late_arrivals alert: a 403 on clear, `can_clear` false, and the alert absent from `?mine=true`.

Use one rule in both the engine and the read condition, so the list, the counts and can_clear still agree:

1. src/shared/alerts/alerts.js mayClear: right after the CEO check, add `if (subjectEmployeeId && user.employee_id && subjectEmployeeId === user.employee_id) return false;`. This mirrors approvers.js and OWN_RECORD, and clear() then answers 403 or 404.
2. src/modules/alerts/alerts.repo.js seenWhere: pass the reader's employee_id in `seen` (readerOf in alerts.service.js already has the user). For a reader who is not the CEO, append `AND a.subject_employee_id IS DISTINCT FROM $n` to the whole condition. The service treats "seen" and "may clear" as the same thing (can_clear = reader.may_clear, needs_you = open), so this one change keeps the following consistent with the engine: the list, one alert (a 404 for one's own alert, per §6), the counts, the Overview's alerts_to_clear, the Open High Alerts card, ⌘K and the assistant.
3. Add the rule to home.md §6 Alerts ("never about the reader themself, the CEO excepted") with a change-log line.
4. Add an integration test: a manager with three late arrivals neither sees nor clears his own alert, while his line manager and Operations still do.

confirmed.title: A sweep or attendance signal that loaded a rule before it was switched off still raises new open alerts on it afterwards
confirmed.scenario: raise() checks only the caller's in-memory `rule.enabled`. sweep() loads every enabled rule once (alerts.sweeps.js:75) and then raises each breach in its own transaction. evaluatePerson works the same way. If an alerts.manage holder sets enabled:false while the 06:00 sweep is part way through that rule (for example a contract_ending rule with two batches of breaches), updateRule commits and closeForRule dismisses the open alerts. Each remaining raise then INSERTs a fresh open alert: its FK KEY SHARE lock only waits for the rule update to commit, and the dismissed rows no longer conflict on the partial unique index. It also emits home.alert_raised, which notifies the grant holders. A probe with a stale enabled row after closeForRule left 1 open alert on a disabled rule. Nothing ever refreshes or dismisses these alerts again, because closeForRule only runs on the on-to-off transition. They stay in Open, Needs You and the chips until someone clears them by hand.
confirmed.fix: Inside raise(), before the INSERT, re-read the rule in the same transaction: `SELECT enabled FROM home_alert_rule WHERE home_alert_rule_id = $1 FOR SHARE`. Return {raised:false} when it is off. FOR SHARE conflicts with updateRule's FOR UPDATE, so a switch-off and a raise are serialised and the raise sees the committed enabled=false.
fixes:
In `raise()` (src/shared/alerts/alerts.js), after the `inTransaction` and rule-id checks and before `evaluate`, `dealtWith` and the INSERT, re-read the rule inside the raise's own transaction and use that fresh copy:

```js
const { rows: [live] } = await client.query(
  `SELECT enabled, threshold, severity, permission_key FROM home_alert_rule
    WHERE home_alert_rule_id = $1 FOR SHARE`,
  [rule.home_alert_rule_id],
);
if (!live || !live.enabled) return { raised: false, created: false, alert: null };
rule = { ...rule, ...live };
```

`rule` is destructured as a parameter, so it can be reassigned; otherwise use a local variable.

Why this works:
- `FOR SHARE` conflicts with the `FOR UPDATE` that `updateRule` takes through `ruleById(..., { lock: true })`. A raise that comes second waits for the switch-off to commit, then sees `enabled=false` (READ COMMITTED re-reads a locked row's latest version).
- A switch-off that comes second waits for the raise to commit, and its `closeForRule` then dismisses the new alert.
- Using the fresh threshold, severity and permission_key also stops a mid-sweep threshold change being judged against the old one.
- Shared locks do not block each other, so concurrent raises are not serialised.

Add an integration case to tests/integration/home-alerts.test.js: raise with a copy of the rule taken before it was switched off, then expect `raised:false` and no open alert on the disabled rule.

- `sweep()` loads the switched-on rules once (src/modules/alerts/alerts.sweeps.js:75) and passes that in-memory row to `runRule`. `runRule` reads the metric batch by batch and raises each breach in its own transaction through `raiseOne`. `evaluatePerson` (line 107) does the same with `enabledRulesFor`.
- `raise()` only checks the caller's copy of the flag (src/shared/alerts/alerts.js:210, `if (!rule.enabled) return ...`). It never re-reads `home_alert_rule`.

  - The foreign key's KEY SHARE check only waits for the rule update to commit.
  - `dealtWith` ignores rule-off closures (`cleared_by IS NOT NULL`), so even a `since` does not suppress the raise.

No interleaving inside a transaction is needed. A user switches rule X off while the sweep is still on an earlier rule (the window is the whole run up to X, and the sweep can be re-run by hand from its queue). The switch-off has fully committed before the sweep reaches X. The sweep then reads X's metric with the stale row and INSERTs fresh open alerts. - raise 1 created an alert;
- `closeForRule` dismissed 1;
- raise 2 with the row loaded before the switch-off returned `raised:true, created:true`;
- the rule then read `enabled:false` with 1 open alert;
- `home.alert_raised` events went from 1 to 2.

- `closeForRule` runs only on the on-to-off transition.
- Later sweeps skip the disabled rule.
- The list, counts and rule queries in alerts.repo.js never filter on `r.enabled`.

confirmed.title: A deadline alert a person cleared is not raised again when the date changes, contrary to home.md §11
confirmed.scenario: For deadline metrics, the evidence `since` is startOfDay(date - threshold). dealtWith suppresses any breach whose since is at or before the latest person-closure. Probe on mycity_e_test: a contract_ending rule with threshold 30, and Ada's contract_ends_on = today+20. The sweep raises the alert, which HR then clears. Then contract_ends_on is brought forward to today+5, and the next sweep reports raised 0 with 0 open alerts. The new since (today-25) is before the clearance, so a contract now ending in 5 days has no alert. A small postponement (+20 to +22) is suppressed the same way. home.md §11 says a cleared deadline alert 'is not raised again unless the date changes'.
confirmed.fix: Make the deadline evidence carry the date itself. For example, have dealtWith (or a deadline-specific branch) treat a closed alert as dealt with only when it was for the same due date, by storing the date on the alert or comparing the closed alert's trigger, which already embeds 'Ends on dd/mm/yyyy'. Alternatively, raise again whenever the due date differs from the one the closed alert was raised for.
fixes:
Key a cleared deadline alert to its due date, not to `since`.

1. Add a nullable `due_on date` column to `home_alert` in Home's M1 migration block, with `-- UP` and `-- DOWN`, idempotent. Document it in docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA.md and home.md §5.
2. In the deadline readings (`deadline()` in alerts.metrics.js), add `due_on` alongside `value` and `since`.
3. Have `alerts.raise` accept `due_on`, write it on INSERT and update it on the ON CONFLICT refresh.
4. In `dealtWith`, when the kind is `deadline`, require the person-closed alert to have the same due date (`AND due_on = $5::date`) instead of `cleared_at >= since`.

The result: the same date is never raised again after a clearance (including when it passes from "Ends" to "Ended"), and any change to the date raises a new alert. This matches home.md §11.

A stopgap with no migration is to compare the closed alert's trigger against `formatDate(due)` (its last 10 characters). That is fragile, so the column is preferable.

Add an integration test: raise a deadline alert, clear it, move the date earlier, sweep, and expect one new alert. Then sweep again with the date unchanged and expect none.

Make a deadline alert record which date it was raised for, and count it as dealt with only for that same date.

Preferred fix (needs a migration; 1150 is merged, so use a new file in Home's block, not an edit to 1150):
1. Add `home_alert.due_on date`, with -- UP and -- DOWN, idempotent.
2. In alerts.metrics.js, have `deadline(rule, today, date)` also return `due_on: date`.
3. Have `raise()` accept `due_on`, write it on INSERT, and keep the ON CONFLICT update as it is.
4. In `dealtWith`, when `due_on` is given, add `AND due_on IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $5::date` to the closed-alert EXISTS. Keep the existing `cleared_at >= since` condition.

Result: the same date is still suppressed, including when "Ends on X" later becomes "Ended on X". A changed date, earlier or later, has no matching closed alert and is raised again, as §11 requires.

Fallback with no schema change: pass `formatDate(due_on)` and match it against the closed alert's trigger with `AND right(trigger, 10) = $5`. Every deadline trigger ends in "on dd/mm/yyyy", but this ties the logic to display copy.

Either way:
- Add an integration case to tests/integration/home-alerts.test.js: clear a contract_ending alert, move contract_ends_on inside the window, sweep, and expect raised 1.
- Tighten the §6 wording in home.md to name the date itself as the deadline evidence.

Make the deadline evidence the due date itself, not a time derived from it.
